statements.status_notes: Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

Upstream GCC commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 sizes the parallel std::search border table one element larger so the border computation cannot index past it. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114690

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. That change resets the stream input pointer and available input after a failed write() in gz_write(), so a later gz* write cannot use the stale caller buffer. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

CVE-2026-33997 (GHSA-pxq6-2prw-chj9) affects privilege comparison during docker plugin install in the Moby daemon's github.com/docker/docker/plugin package. Prometheus 3.11.3 imports github.com/docker/docker only for Docker and Swarm service discovery; its production dependency graph includes Docker API types and the client package, but not github.com/docker/docker/plugin or daemon packages. The image does not ship dockerd, so the vulnerable plugin-manager code is not present in the shipped Prometheus binaries.

CVE-2026-93687 affects the npm braces package at 3.0.3, the latest release on the public npm registry, so no patched version is available yet. On Prometheus 3.x stable lines the component appears in the SPDX SBOM for bundled web UI static assets built from the prometheus package; the durable remediation is a dependency override in the prometheus HSP package build once upstream publishes a fix. Reachability of the vulnerable recursion path in the shipped static UI bundle is under assessment.

The covered package builds prevent a failed direct-buffer gzwrite from leaving a caller-owned input pointer available to gzprintf or gzvprintf. They either guard the later formatting entry points or include the pointer-state reset from upstream commit https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148 in the equivalent zlib 1.3.1 error branch. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85091.

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree, which is frozen upstream with no fixed module release; see https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5932. The docker-engine APK ships dockerd built from Moby 29.7.2, which vendors github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto for OpenPGP and does not import golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp. go version -m on the published dockerd binary lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 as a module dependency but no golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp import path, so the advisory OpenPGP code is not present in the shipped artifact.

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package and its subpackages (openpgp, openpgp/packet, openpgp/armor, openpgp/clearsign, openpgp/errors, openpgp/elgamal, openpgp/s2k), which are unmaintained with no fixed version. Neither prometheus nor promtool imports any openpgp subpackage: go list -deps ./cmd/prometheus and ./cmd/promtool at v3.5.5 and v3.13.2 (x/crypto 0.55.0) resolve only cryptobyte, chacha20poly1305, bcrypt, blowfish, pkcs12, and hkdf from golang.org/x/crypto. The dhi/prometheus-nats-exporter image installs the prometheus-nats-exporter package and ships only /usr/bin/prometheus-nats-exporter; go list -deps at upstream v0.20.2 resolves bcrypt, blake2b, blowfish, chacha20, chacha20poly1305, curve25519, nacl/box, nacl/secretbox, ocsp, and salsa20/salsa from golang.org/x/crypto with no openpgp subpackage. The dhi/prometheus-adapter image installs the prometheus-adapter package and ships only /usr/bin/adapter; go list -deps ./cmd/adapter at upstream v0.12.0 resolves cryptobyte, hkdf, nacl/secretbox, and salsa20/salsa from golang.org/x/crypto with no openpgp subpackage. The dhi/prometheus-config-reloader image ships only the prometheus-config-reloader binary (Alpine installs the prometheus-config-reloader package; Debian builds ./cmd/prometheus-config-reloader from prometheus-operator); go list -deps ./cmd/prometheus-config-reloader at upstream v0.94.1 resolves bcrypt, blowfish, chacha20, chacha20poly1305, cryptobyte, and internal poly1305/alias from golang.org/x/crypto with no openpgp subpackage. Go dead-code elimination means the vulnerable openpgp code is not compiled into the shipped binaries. Scout matches at the module level because the advisory records golang.org/x/crypto with no fixed version.
